subject: Account sunset: proposed SLA & backup constraints follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alison Reed <areed@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap / account sunset requirements (PII, backups, timeline)

Hi Alison — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before I loop in Legal/Presales: 

Summary of requirements we captured on the call:
- FinTechCo needs an account-sunset/RTBF flow for user-initiated deletion (web UI + API) that covers PII fields and derived embeddings.
- Retention constraints: production data must be logically deleted within 24 hours of a validated request. Backups are subject to your internal retention policy (you indicated 180 days for backup rotations).
- Logging/audit: you need attestations that deletion actions are logged (who/when/request id) and an export for compliance reviews.
- Residency: customer data stored in us-west region; you confirmed no cross-region moves.

Open questions from Redwood: 
1) Can FinTechCo accept logical expunge from active stores plus a defined schedule for backup purge (e.g., next backup rotation) rather than immediate physical removal from immutable backup copies?
2) Are there regulatory reasons (e.g., pending investigations) that would prevent scheduled backup purges inside 180 days?
3) Do you require a formal SLA for time-to-delete from active stores and for final purge from backups? If so, what target (24h/72h/other)?

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan) / next steps:
- Redwood: provide a draft MAP with timeline and technical approach for active-store logical deletion, backup purge guidance, and logging artifacts by Nov 10. (I attached a short playbook + retention matrix.)
- FinTechCo: confirm any legal holds or investigations that would extend backup retention and share the desired SLA for active-store delete.
- Joint: sign-off on MAP and attach as an addendum to the order/contract.

Attachments: backup-retention-matrix.csv (simple mapping of store vs backup retention), data-purge-playbook-v1.pdf (technical steps + audit fields).

Thanks — I’m aiming to get the draft MAP out by EOD Nov 10.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Alison Reed <areed@fintechco.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap / account sunset requirements (PII, backups, timeline)

Vanessa — thanks for the tidy summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Backup retention: our standard is 180 days, but Legal flagged that certain accounts (e.g., under audit or subject to litigation holds) may be retained longer. We need to surface any hold flags as part of the MAP.
- Immediate physical purge from backups: that’s not feasible for us because our backup images are immutable and stored offsite; we can schedule targeted purges only at rotation windows. For a given dataset, purging typically occurs at the next rotation that affects that archive window (we estimate 30–90 days depending on archive tier).
- Active-store deletion SLA: 24 hours is ambitious but acceptable as a target for verified requests; Legal would like it stated as "best-effort 24 hours, with documented exceptions."
- Audit exports: agreed — we need a downloadable CSV with deletion event id, user id, request timestamp, actor, and confirmation of affected artifacts (embeddings, model cache keys).

I’ll confirm if any active holds apply for the accounts in scope. If none, we can accept the logical-delete-plus-scheduled-backup-purge approach. Please include a clause about rotations and hold-exceptions in the MAP.

— Alison
Director, Infrastructure Security | FinTechCo
areed@fintechco.com | +1 206-555-0199

On Nov 07, 2026, at 09:12, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> (See above)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap / account sunset requirements (PII, backups, timeline)

Vanessa — quick technical notes to feed into the MAP: 

- Active-store expunge: we can implement a two-step expunge flow. Step 1 (logical): remove PII and replace with hashed token, evict embeddings and KV cache, and mark record state="deleted". Step 2 (physical): a background job runs to zero-out storage blocks prior to backup rotation when possible.
- Backups: we treat backups as immutable snapshots. For nearline/archival backups we can annotate metadata in the snapshot index indicating a purge request; then on next lifecycle job we exclude those objects. That yields the 30–90 day window Alison mentioned.
- Audit logs: we’ll emit an event per delete request with request_id and operator; we can provide a daily export for compliance.
- Edge case: if customer has exported model snapshots referencing user content (e.g., finetune artifacts) those need explicit coordination to remove copies. Add as an explicit checklist item.

I’ll add these as bullet points in the MAP draft. We can offer an "accelerated purge" program for enterprise customers that commits a short-term retention for backups in exchange for a contractual fee and operational coordination (we've used this before when customers need faster physical purge timelines).

— Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alison Reed <areed@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Draft MAP: account sunset & purge approach (attached)

Alison / Legal — attaching the draft MAP for your review. Key proposals in short: 

1) Active-store deletion: Redwood performs verified logical deletion within 24 hours. Verification = request + account owner confirmation + request id stored.
2) Backup purge: Redwood will annotate backup snapshots with purge markers; physical removal occurs at next applicable backup rotation (expected 30–90 days depending on tier). For accounts under legal hold, the hold window supersedes purge schedule and will be called out in the MAP.
3) Auditability: daily export of deletion events (CSV) containing request_id, operator, timestamp, data types removed, and confirmation flags.
4) Exceptions & accelerated purge: accelerated purge can be provided as a paid service with operational coordination; otherwise standard rotation windows apply.

Action items: 
- FinTechCo Legal: confirm whether existing holds apply to the accounts in scope and provide any required hold-notice text we should mirror.
- FinTechCo Security: confirm acceptance of the 24h logical-delete SLA as "best-effort" and the backup purge cadence (30–90 days).
- Redwood: if accepted, we will prepare a short contract addendum (MAP) and a sample clause for the MSA describing backup rotations and hold exceptions.

Attachments: data-purge-playbook-v1.pdf, backup-retention-matrix.csv

If this looks good, I’ll prepare the MSA clause and share a DocuSign link.

— Vanessa

From: Alison Reed <areed@fintechco.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: FinTechCo Legal <legal@fintechco.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: account sunset & purge approach (attached)

Thanks Vanessa — this addresses our concerns. Legal confirms no active holds for the pilot accounts. We accept the logical-delete within 24 hours (documented as best-effort) and the backup purge cadence as described, with the understanding that FinTechCo will request accelerated purge for any high-risk incidents and Redwood will quote cost and timeline.

Please send the MSA clause and DocuSign link for the MAP addendum; once that’s in place we’ll schedule a short runbook review with our Ops team.

— Alison
